title: Canonical cochain multiplication of a lattice equivariant algebra
statement: Let R be a commutative condensed ring on the fixed small profinite site [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] and let E=Action(Mod_R,Z^r) be the ordinary discrete lattice action category [lem-sfb-discrete-lattice-koszul-resolution]. Use the canonical additive monoidal and derived structures supplied by [def-sfb-lattice-derived-invariants-tensor]. An equivariant unital algebra is Mon(E). Fix the canonical signed total cochain tensor and its module, action, homotopy and derived tensor presentations. For each algebra B, there exists a unique chain map tensorObj(B[0],B[0]) to B[0] whose restriction to the (0,0) summand, under the canonical single-complex identifications, is the original multiplication of B. The cochain monoidal tensor is definitionally tensorObj. These constructions require neither nonzero coefficients nor flatness of B or R.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-expanded ordinary lattice input: canonical algebra-valued cup construction used in proof steps 9 and 13 of lem-sfb-lattice-koszul-triangulated-cup-comparison

proof.text: The selected cochain monoidal tensor is definitionally HomologicalComplex.tensorObj, so cochainTensor_eq is reflexivity.

For S=B[0], a summand S.X p tensor S.X q is a zero object whenever p or q is nonzero, because tensoring preserves zero objects. Coproduct extensionality then proves the total tensor has zero terms outside degree zero.

Use mapBifunctorDesc to define the degree-zero map by the original multiplication on the (0,0) summand and zero on every other summand. The degree -1 source is zero, so mkHomToSingle extends this map to a chain map. The inclusion computation rule and the canonical inverse isomorphisms give the multiplication equation.

A map to a single complex is determined in degree zero. Coproduct extensionality reduces uniqueness to the (p,q) summands. All summands with p nonzero have zero source; if p=0 then p+q=0 gives q=0, where the normalization equation and cancellation of canonical isomorphisms prove equality.

proof_origin.place: Paragraph (3), proof step 13; the existing single-multiplication docstring argument, formalized by G4 using coproduct descent and single-complex extensionality.

lean.statement:
theorem singleMultiplicationExists (B : Algebra R r) :
    ∃! m : HomologicalComplex.tensorObj
        ((HomologicalComplex.single (Equivariant R r) (.up ℤ) 0).obj B.X)
        ((HomologicalComplex.single (Equivariant R r) (.up ℤ) 0).obj B.X) ⟶
        (HomologicalComplex.single (Equivariant R r) (.up ℤ) 0).obj B.X,
      (MonoidalCategoryStruct.tensorHom (C := Equivariant R r)
        (HomologicalComplex.singleObjXSelf (.up ℤ) 0 B.X).inv
        (HomologicalComplex.singleObjXSelf (.up ℤ) 0 B.X).inv) ≫
      HomologicalComplex.ιTensorObj
        ((HomologicalComplex.single (Equivariant R r) (.up ℤ) 0).obj B.X)
        ((HomologicalComplex.single (Equivariant R r) (.up ℤ) 0).obj B.X) 0 0 0 rfl ≫ m.f 0 ≫
      (HomologicalComplex.singleObjXSelf (.up ℤ) 0 B.X).hom =
        MonObj.mul (X := B.X)
